task.title: Track and Finish an In-Progress Operation
task.shortdesc: See where a paused merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert stands, then abort, restart, or continue it.

context.p:
When an operation pauses for conflicts, the Git Client shows where it stands. The view labels the operation in progress (for example, Merging), and the view marks the commits involved with amber labels: your current commit is Start (Mine), and the incoming side is labeled by operation — Incoming (Theirs) for a merge, HEAD for a rebase, Cherry-picked commit, or Reverted commit. A dashed grey line connects the source commit to the branch's
node.

fig.title: In-Progress Merge in the Git History View

step.cmd: Resolve any conflicts the operation reported.
From the conflict panel, finish or back out of the operation.

choices.choice: Continue — completes the operation once every conflict is resolved.
Abort — cancels the operation and restores the state from before it started.

info.p: You can abort or restart at any time before you commit.
